
Axis bank was established in 1993 as UTI Bank, and is now the third largest private sector bank in India, following HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank. The reach comes with that rank as it has the third largest branch network of private banks and is also present in international locations such as DIFC (Dubai), Singapore and GIFT City. It acquired Citibank India's consumer business in 2023 as its biggest strategic acquisition in recent years. That agreement attracted rich customers and a good credit card customer base. It is why Axis is where it is now in terms of credit cards and money. 

Axis Bank is a part of Nifty 50s. This is what it appeared as at the end of the quarter of June 2026:

Share price on NSE just before results is ₹1,328
Price to Earning ratio of about 15.7x, a discount to HDFC Bank (16.6x), ICICI Bank (19.1x) and Kotak Bank(20.1x) 
Price to Book Value of about 2.0x 

The balance sheet looks good as the capital adequacy ratio stood at 16.67% and CET-1 at 14.64% which were both far above the regulatory requirements. Part of this discount is due to profitability as returns remain lower for Axis than ICICI Bank's. 

The company's profitability has been on the rise steadily, though margins are under strain. However, Axis Bank posted standalone net profit of ₹7,114 crore in Q1 FY27, which was 23% higher than the figure of ₹5,806 crore in the previous year. The bottom line is more complicated: 

Net interest income grew by 8% to ₹14,646 crore 
The core operating profit increased by 10% to reach ₹11,122 crore. 
Net interest margin (NIM) narrowed to 3.46% from 3.80% in a year ago. 

The margin story is most important for a customer profitability study. Loans increased at a higher rate than the availability of cheap money. Net advances grew 19% to ₹12.6 lakh crore, but CASA deposits grew only 11.4% while term deposits grew 22.8%. This was a drop from the 39.6% recorded in the previous quarter, and was the lowest value recorded for the CASA ratio since the first quarter of 2017. It means that Axis Bank is lending the money at a higher cost. A customer with a loan, a credit card and a CASA balance is much more lucrative than a non-deposit customer who has a loan.

A positive aspect is asset quality. Gross NPA fell to 1.28% and net NPA to 0.39%, with net credit cost at 0.63%. Thus, less defaults are costing customers money. 

Axis Bank offers 
-Retail loans like home loans, personal loans, auto loans, two-wheeler loans, loans against property, gold loans, education loans and loans against securities.
-Business and corporate loans like working capital, term loans and MSME credit. During Q1 of FY27, the total volume of corporate advances increased by 38% yoy. 
-Flipkart, Ace, Airtel, Magnus, and Reserve are all offering credit cards, ranging from mass to premium. In Q1 FY27, Axis issued 0.92 million new cards, and currently has 13.4% of cards in force. 
-Non-bank arms: Axis Finance earned a profit of ₹244 crore, which is 29% higher.

The three sources of Axis Bank's earnings are loan interest, card fees and cheap CASA funds. To know where the bank makes money you need to know what types of customers are paired with these services.
